reviews.decision_reason: map_coverage preserves the downstream needs handoff, maps only exact need-to-capability matches, and leaves unmatched needs as unsupported. The observed coverage output has direct coverage only for the six supplied capabilities and unsupported coverage for n06-r01 and n06-r07.

prioritize_needs contains the behaviorally significant root fault: it sets unsupported to true when coverage == 'direct'. This contradicts its role to rank unsupported needs before covered needs and causes covered capability matches to be prioritized ahead of genuinely unsupported demand records. The final priorities show direct-covered n06-r02 through n06-r06 and n06-r08 marked unsupported:true, while genuinely unsupported n06-r01 and n06-r07 are pushed to priorities 7 and 8.

synthesize_recommendation retains the eight-item priority window and derives the recommendation from the first already-ranked priority record as declared. The bad recommendation is downstream of the inverted unsupported flag produced by prioritize_needs, not a separate synthesis fault.

select_demand_records preserves the explicit fallback path and selects all supplied demanded rows in the corpus. No generic keyword-only or unrelated-candidate issue is visible in this boundary from the supplied package.

normalize_evidence keeps the bounded allowed-record window, normalizes missing fields with neutral sentinels, and passes forward the eight expected needs. No contradictory or missing transformation evidence is visible for this boundary.

assemble_provenance builds the expected ranked evidence-source handoff from normalized needs. The downstream evidence_sources handoff hash matches between producer and consumer, so the fault is not in provenance assembly or handoff integrity.
